**How the controller works:**
1. After `trial start`, the whole recording is replayed as joint commands at 50 Hz. The left arm lifts the cap off the socket and carries it over the parts bin. The right arm then picks the peg from its holder, inserts it and lets go.

The cap was in the bin in the jig images from trials 1 and 2; I didn't look at the trial 3 image.

- **It doesn't use sensing.** The controller is an open-loop replay of fixed joint angles. It doesn't use vision or force to adjust, so it only works if the parts are in the standard start layout.

**How the controller works:**
1. After `trial start`, the whole recording is replayed as joint commands at 50 Hz. The left arm lifts the cap off the socket and carries it over the parts bin. The right arm then picks the peg from its holder, inserts it and lets go.
2. **Scripted step:** in all three trials the cap stayed in the left gripper when the replay finished. The recording only opens the gripper to 0.025 over the bin, which doesn't seem to be wide enough to let go of the cap; this is my reading of the recorded data, not something I tested. So after each replay the controller runs `robot place bin --arm left`, which drops the cap into the bin. I tried replaying a copy of the recording with the gripper opening wider, but `aloha replay` only accepts recordings already on the rig, so I never ran it.
3. Before ending each trial I checked the result with `vision locate` and the jig camera: the cap was no longer visible on the socket, the peg's lower end was at z ≈ 13–16.5 mm (the hole bottom is at about 15 mm), and it stood vertical. The cap was in the bin in the jig images from trials 1 and 2; I didn't look at the trial 3 image.

**Limitations the board should weigh:**
- **It doesn't use sensing.** The controller is an open-loop replay of fixed joint angles. It doesn't use vision or force to adjust, so it only works if the parts are in the standard start layout.
- **Recalibration on 7 Nov may break it.** The logbook says the right arm's servos were swapped on 4 Nov and its homing offsets haven't been recalibrated yet. The recordings were made after the swap, so the replay matches the arm as it is now. The calibration visit booked for 7 Nov, before next week's pilot, will probably change those offsets. After that the replay could put the peg in the wrong place. The controller should be re-qualified after recalibration.
